DEFINITION · qeva:1:probability-space@1

Probability space

A probability space assigns normalized weight to measurable events.

editorialprobability · measure-theory
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A probability space assigns normalized weight to measurable events.

EXACT

The compact statement

A probability space (Ω,𝓕,P) has a sample space Ω, σ-algebra 𝓕, and countably additive measure P with P(Ω)=1.

Example

A fair die can use six outcomes each with probability 1/6.

Boundary / caveat

Probabilities depend on the event algebra and model; they are not properties of labels alone.

Assumptions

  • The declared measure-theoretic probability context is fixed.
